headline: Floating Boardwalks and Parabolic Dunes of PEI
reservation: Access to Greenwich is part of Prince Edward Island National Park; a park pass is required for entry. While the beach and trails are open to the public, seasonal interpretive programs may require separate registration. Check the Parks Canada website for the current fee structure and pass validation locations.

days.title: The Floating Boardwalk and Dunes
days.start: Suggested: 9:00 AM from Greenwich Interpretive Centre

stops.name: Greenwich Dunes Trail
stops.detail: Walk through old farm fields and forest before crossing the stunning floating boardwalk over Bowley Pond.

stops.name: The Parabolic Dunes
stops.detail: Observe the rare, shifting sand formations from the designated viewing platforms at the end of the boardwalk.

days.driving: Walking only once at the site; allow 2 hours for the round trip
days.note: Stay on the designated boardwalks to protect the extremely fragile dune ecosystem from erosion.

days.title: Coastal Heritage and Bays
days.start: Suggested: 10:00 AM from St. Peters Bay

stops.name: Greenwich Interpretive Centre
stops.detail: Engage with interactive exhibits that explain the 10,000-year history of human habitation in this region.

stops.name: Tlaqatik Trail
stops.detail: A loop trail offering views of St. Peters Bay, highlighting the area's importance to Mi'kmaw culture.

days.driving: Allow 15 minutes from St. Peters Bay; conditions vary
days.note: Wind off the bay can be brisk; a windbreaker is recommended even on sunny days.

days.title: Beach Exploration

stops.name: Greenwich Beach
stops.detail: Relax on the supervised swimming area characterized by fine white sand and warmer Gulf Stream waters.

stops.name: Havre Saint Pierre Trail
stops.detail: A short walk through the woods and fields that offers a glimpse into the Acadian history of the peninsula.

days.driving: Minimal; parking is central to both the beach and trailheads
days.note: Beach supervision is seasonal; check the Parks Canada site for lifeguard duty dates.

intel.title: Arrival Logistics
intel.text: The main parking lot at the Interpretive Centre serves as the hub for all trails. It can fill during July and August afternoons, so mid-morning arrival is advised.

intel.title: Trail Surfaces
intel.text: The Greenwich Dunes Trail features crushed gravel and a floating boardwalk. It is generally accessible, but heavy rains can occasionally cause soft spots near the pond edges.

intel.title: Nearby Services
intel.text: The nearest fuel and full-service grocery stores are located in St. Peters Bay or Morell. There are no convenience services within the National Park boundaries.

intel.title: Network Coverage
intel.text: Signal is reliable near the Interpretive Centre but may fade as you move toward the dunes. Do not rely on GPS for finding trailhead markers; use the official park maps.

intel.title: Seasonal Facilities
intel.text: The Interpretive Centre and washroom facilities have specific seasonal dates, typically operating from June to September. Outside of these months, the trails remain open but services are unavailable.

plan.arrival: Collect your vehicle at Charlottetown Airport (YYG) and drive 50 minutes east. Stop in Morell for beach supplies and local seafood before checking into your accommodation near St. Peters Bay.
plan.vehicle: Any standard rental car is suitable for the well-maintained paved roads leading to Greenwich. No off-road capability is required.
plan.goldenHour: The viewing platform at the end of the Dunes Trail offers an unobstructed west-facing view for sunset over the Gulf of St. Lawrence.
